definitions.explanation: a baseball bat made of metal, typically aluminum alloy, used widely in amateur baseball in Japan

examples.japanese: {金属|きんぞく}バット⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{打|う}つ→打つ：01221_utsu⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{音|おと}→音：00743_oto⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{違|ちが}う→違う：01957_chigau⟧。
examples.english: It sounds different when you hit with a metal bat.

examples.japanese: ⟦{高校|こうこう}{野球|やきゅう}→高校野球：21950_koukouyakyuu⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{金属|きんぞく}バット⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{使|つか}われている→使う：00473_tsukau⟧。

examples.japanese: {金属|きんぞく}バット⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{木製|もくせい}→木製：13083_mokusei_b⟧⟦バット→バット：11590_batto⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{比|くら}べて→比べる：01237_kuraberu⟧⟦{折|お}れ→折れる：01266_oreru⟧にくく、{飛距離|ひきょり}⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{出|で}→出る：00513_deru⟧やすい。
examples.english: Metal bats are less likely to break than wooden bats, and the ball also tends to travel farther.

notes:
The standard bat type in Japanese amateur baseball, from Little League through high school. Composed of ⟦{金属|きんぞく}→金属：02645_kinzoku⟧ (metal) + ⟦バット→バット：11590_batto⟧ (bat). Professional baseball (⟦プロ{野球|やきゅう}→プロ野球：08837_puroyakyuu⟧) requires ⟦{木製|もくせい}→木製：13083_mokusei_b⟧⟦バット→バット：11590_batto⟧ (wooden bats), so the transition from metal to wood is a major challenge for players entering the pros.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {金属|きんぞく}バット⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{打|う}つ→打つ：01221_utsu⟧ — to hit with a metal bat
- {金属|きんぞく}バット⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{打球音|だきゅうおん} — the sound of a hit off a metal bat (the distinctive "ping")
- {金属|きんぞく}バット⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{重|おも}さ→重さ：14444_omosa⟧ — the weight of a metal bat

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{木製|もくせい}→木製：13083_mokusei_b⟧⟦バット→バット：11590_batto⟧ — wooden bat (required in professional baseball)
- ⟦バット→バット：11590_batto⟧ — bat (general term)
- ⟦{複合|ふくごう}→複合：14114_fukugou⟧⟦バット→バット：11590_batto⟧ — composite bat

CULTURAL NOTE:
⟦{甲子園|こうしえん}→甲子園：23102_koushien⟧ (the national high school baseball tournament) is synonymous with {金属|きんぞく}バット in Japan. The distinctive metallic ping of contact is one of the iconic sounds of summer.
